http://www.wizards.com/DCI
(under "tournament rules" - see both the universal rules and the
V:TES-specific rules)

On section (737) of the V:TES rules is missing from the on-line document
(although it is present in the printed document that the DCI sent
to its registered judges). This section deals with Rochester Draft, so
it doesn't apply to the Origins event (which is a Booster Draft), but
here it is anyhow:

737. Rules for V:TES Rochester Draft Tournaments
This rule works in conjunction with Section 77 and 78 of the Universal
Tournament Rules.

Players open their first booster packs when the pod judge instructs them
to do so. After counting the cards face-down to make sure the pack is
correct, players then move all vampire (crypt) cards to the top of the
pack face-down. If players do not have the appropriate number of cards in
a pack, they must immediately notify the head judge, who will replace the
pack.

Players then place their opened packs face-down on the table in front of
them. At a signal from the pod judge, players place the top two cards from
their booster pack [sic] face-up on the table. The pod judge then has
players draft according to section 77 and 78 of the Universal Tournament
Rules until the packs are completely drafted.

--
LSJ (vte...@white-wolf.com) V:TES Net.Rep for White Wolf, Inc.
Links to revised rulebook, rulings, errata, and tournament rules:
http://www.geocities.com/vtesrep

Messages.Author: Madman2001
Messages.Body:
LSJ:

I could not find a reference at this URL to what players use to make
their decks during the Sealed tournament. I had heard somewhere -
probably here :) - that it was a starter and 2 boosters. At least that
is implied under the Universal Tournament rules.

Also, I presume that the Booster Draft will follow the same format as a
Magic:tG Booster Draft??

Let me know, please and thanks.

Assuming that the preceding is true, I do respectfully think that these
formats are not the best fit for V:TES. While these formats work well
for Magic, the resultant V:TES decks are weaker than they should/could
be.

I realize we've had this discussion before (are there any original
discussions left in this game?), and, to some extent, it doesn't make a
lot of difference so long as there is a level playing field.
Nonetheless, it is more fun to play with smoother deck, so that for
example, you're not stuck with a fist full of Potence cards while all
you have in play are Malkavians.

Anyway, my $0.02. I'll see you there!!!

It is whatever the coordinator chooses (as in Draft). In the case of
the V:TES Sealed game on Friday at Origins, WotC will be providing
1 V:TES starter and 3 V:TES base set boosters per player.

> Also, I presume that the Booster Draft will follow the same format as a
> Magic:tG Booster Draft??

Only inasfar as they both follow the Universal Booster Draft rules.
[DCI UTR 74]

The only V:TES-specific rule regarding limited-format play is the
deck size rule (40 - 90 cards in the library, standard 12+ crypt).
[DCI VTES 731]

> Nonetheless, it is more fun to play with smoother deck, so that for
> example, you're not stuck with a fist full of Potence cards while all
> you have in play are Malkavians.

In sealed deck play, there is no way to alter this situation, other than
having the coordinator provide vampires they way MTG coordinator provide
basic land.

In draft play, it would be wiser not to draft a "fist full of Potence
cards" while also drafting nothing but Malkavians, IMO. That decision is
ultimately left to the player, though.
